difficulty.explanation: Difficulty is calculated using **effort distance**: the trail distance plus elevation gain divided by 100. For road running, only distance is used. Thresholds vary by activity type.
difficulty.formula: **Effort distance** = distance (km) + elevation gain (m) ÷ 100. For example, a 15 km trail with 800 m gain = 23 km effort.

paceModel.explanation: Time estimates are based on a modified Naismith's Rule. Flat speed varies by activity type, with extra time added per 100 m of elevation gain. Actual times will vary with fitness, terrain, and conditions.
paceModel.formula: **Time** = distance ÷ flat speed + elevation gain × climb penalty. For example, a 10 km trail run with 500 m gain ≈ 86 min + 15 min = ~1h 41m.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Answers to common questions about trails, times, and events on Hlaupadagskra.is

estimatedTime.q: How is Estimated Time for trails calculated?
estimatedTime.a: See the model below. Times are estimates only — actual time depends on fitness, terrain conditions, and weather.

terrainType.q: How is the terrain type (Flat / Hilly / Mountainous) decided?
terrainType.a: Terrain type is calculated automatically from the trail's GPS data using two factors: elevation gain per km (climb ratio) and maximum altitude above sea level. Flat: less than 20 m of gain per km. Mountainous: reaches above 600 m altitude with at least 30 m/km gain, or any trail climbing more than 50 m per km. Hilly: everything in between. Thresholds are calibrated for Icelandic conditions.

relatedTrails.a: Related trails are ranked by a scoring system. Trails that are part of the same series score highest. Points are then added for shared locations (area), shared tags, and the same activity type. Only trails with at least one matching factor are shown.

difficulty.q: How is difficulty (Easy / Moderate / Hard / Expert / Extreme) calculated?
difficulty.a: Difficulty is based on an effort distance formula: effort = distance (km) + elevation gain (m) ÷ 100. This combines length and climbing into a single number that is then compared against thresholds tuned per activity type. Trail running and hiking thresholds are lower than cycling, for example, since the effort per km is greater. Road running, fun runs, and obstacle courses use distance only, since they typically have little elevation.

itraIndex.q: What is the ITRA Performance Index?
itraIndex.a: The ITRA Performance Index is a personal score (0–1000) that reflects your racing potential. Every time you finish an ITRA-certified race, you receive a Race Score based on your speed relative to a theoretical world-record pace on that course. Your Performance Index is the weighted average of your best 5 Race Scores over the last 36 months. Some races, like Laugavegur Ultra Trail, require a minimum index of 370 to enter. See the full guide for details.

gpsDistance.q: How accurate is the trail length?
gpsDistance.a: Distances are calculated directly from the trail's GPX file using the coordinates of the recorded route. The accuracy depends on the quality of the source GPX — a well-recorded GPS track is typically accurate to within 1–2%. Distances are shown rounded to one decimal place.

trailSuggestion.q: Can I suggest a trail or send a correction?
trailSuggestion.a: Yes — use the tip button on any trail page to send a suggestion, correction, or additional information. For a brand new trail, you can also reach us via the contact page.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Hlaupadagskra.is is committed to respecting your privacy. This policy explains what data we collect, how we use it, and your rights. The short version: we collect very little and share nothing.

noAccounts.title: No User Accounts Required
noAccounts.body: The public Hlaupadagskra.is website does not require you to create an account or log in. We do not collect your name, email address, or any personal information to use the site.

viewTracking.title: Trail View Tracking
viewTracking.body: When you view a trail, we record the visit to show trending and popular trails. We store a one-way hash of your IP address — not the IP itself — to prevent duplicate counting. This hash cannot be reversed to identify you. View data is used solely for aggregate statistics (e.g., "most viewed trails this week").

localStorage.title: Data Stored on Your Device
localStorage.body: Your favorites, hidden trails, language preference, and dark/light mode setting are stored locally on your device using browser localStorage. This data never leaves your device and is not sent to our servers. You can clear it at any time through your browser settings.

thirdParty.title: Third-Party Services
thirdParty.body: Weather forecasts are fetched from Open-Meteo via our backend — your IP is not exposed to Open-Meteo. Map tiles are served by OpenStreetMap. We do not use any analytics services (no Google Analytics, no tracking pixels), no advertising networks, and no cookies. We do not sell or share any data with third parties.

privacy.contact: Questions about privacy? Reach out to us through the About page.

useAtOwnRisk.title: Use at Your Own Risk
useAtOwnRisk.body: All trail information on Hlaupadagskra.is is provided for informational purposes only. You are solely responsible for your own safety when using any trail. Always assess conditions, your fitness level, and equipment before heading out. Hlaupadagskra.is is not liable for any injuries, accidents, damages, or losses arising from the use of the information on this site.

weather.title: Weather & Conditions
weather.body: Weather forecasts are sourced from Open-Meteo and may not be accurate. Conditions in Iceland can change rapidly and without warning. The trail condition indicators (Good, Fair, Poor) are automated estimates and should not be your sole source of information. Always check official weather forecasts from vedur.is before heading into the mountains.

accuracy.title: GPS Data & Accuracy
accuracy.body: Trail distances, elevation profiles, and GPS tracks are approximate and derived from GPX data. Actual trail conditions, distances, and difficulty may differ from what is shown. Trail markings and routes may change over time. Always carry proper navigation tools and know how to use them.

emergency.title: Emergency Information
emergency.body: In an emergency in Iceland, call 112. The Icelandic Association for Search and Rescue (ICE-SAR) operates rescue services nationwide. Before heading out, leave your travel plan at safetravel.is and consider downloading the 112 Iceland app.

itra.guideLabel: Our quick guide: Understanding the ITRA System

itraGuide.title: 🏃‍♂️ Quick Guide: Understanding the ITRA System
itraGuide.intro: If you are confused by how ITRA scores work, you are not alone. Here is a clear breakdown of the 5 key concepts you need to know, using a simple "Distance vs. Speed" logic.

concepts.title: ITRA Endurance Points (The "Length" Metric)
items: 📌 What it is: A difficulty score assigned to a specific race route based only on distance and elevation. It ranges from 0 to 6.
⚙️ How it works: Think of this as a pass/fail completion badge. Everyone who crosses the finish line gets the exact same points, whether they came in 1st place or last place.
💡 Keep in mind: Short races (like an 8km or 16km) usually award 0 ITRA Points. This does not mean the race doesn't count — it just means it is a short distance.

concepts.title: ITRA Performance Index (The "Speed" Metric)
items: 📌 What it is: Your personal global ranking score, ranging from 0 to 1000. It represents your theoretical maximum racing potential.

⚙️ How it works: Every time you finish an ITRA-certified race, you receive a personal Race Score based purely on your speed compared to a theoretical world-record pace on that specific course. Your overall Performance Index is the weighted average of your up to 5 best Race Scores over the last 36 months.

🏔️ The Laugavegur Rule: To enter the Laugavegur Ultra Trail, organizers don't care how many ITRA Points you have. They strictly require an ITRA Performance Index of 370 or higher. This proves you have the physical engine and speed to clear the mountain safety time limits. (For context, finishing the 55km Laugavegur course in 9 hours and 15 minutes equals roughly a 370 score).

concepts.title: Mountain Level (The "Steepness" Metric)
items: 📌 What it is: A difficulty rating from 0 to 12 that tells you how technical and steep the terrain is.

⚙️ How it works: A 1 means flat roads or smooth paths. A 12 means extreme mountain terrain with massive, steep climbs and technical footing. It helps you understand what kind of gear and training you need for the terrain.

concepts.title: Finisher Level (The "Cut-Off" Metric)
items: 📌 What it is: The minimum personal Performance Index a runner needs to have to successfully cross the finish line before the time limit expires.

⚙️ How it works: If a race has a Finisher Level of 220, a runner with a personal index of 220 will likely finish right at the final cut-off second. If it is 0, the time limit is exceptionally generous.

concepts.title: National League (The "Local Leaderboard")
items: 📌 What it is: A yearly ranking system that stacks you up against other runners in your home country.

⚙️ How it works: It automatically updates every calendar year. If you run at least 3 ITRA-certified races in your own country during the year, your top 3 scores are aggregated to rank you on your local national leaderboard.

section370.title: What does it take to reach a 370 Performance Index?
section370.p1: To unlock a 370 ITRA Performance Index score, you need to maintain a flat-equivalent pace of roughly 5:45 to 6:00 per kilometer.
section370.p2: Because trail races have hills, ITRA evaluates your speed using Effort-Kilometers (Effort-KM). The formula adds 1 kilometer of distance for every 100 meters of climbing. To reach a 370 score, you need an average pace of roughly 6:00 to 6:15 per Effort-KM.

table.title: Target Finish Times for a 370 ITRA Score

runningTrip.title: Running Trip in the Swiss Alps
